get.description:
Returns the current quotes for one item across marketplaces, identified by its Steam market hash name.

- The result has at most one quote per market and side, sorted by `market_code` and then `side`. When several sources report the same market, a quote that is still listed takes precedence over a delisted one, then data taken directly from that marketplace over aggregators, then the most recently confirmed quote (`fresh_at`) wins.
- A market is reported as delisted (`delisted_at` set, `quantity` `0`, last known price kept) only when every source for it has delisted the item.
- Items with enough market data also get one `CSCP` quote with `side` `mid`: the cs.cheap valuation, a weighted consensus of the marketplaces' sell listings and buy orders in CNY, refreshed once a day. Its `valuation` object carries the confidence (`credibility`, `uncertainty`) and the two consensus prices; on every other quote `valuation` is `null`. It is an estimate, not a tradable offer.
- Narrow the result with `markets` (comma-separated market codes; `CSCP` selects the valuation) and `side` (`ask`, `bid`, `mid` or `all`).
- `market_hash_name` must match exactly, including case.
- Prices are decimal strings in each marketplace's own currency (`market_currency_code`); nothing is converted.
- `404` means the item has no quotes at all for this `app_id`. An item whose quotes are all excluded by `markets` or `side` returns `200` with an empty `markets` list.

> [!note]
> This endpoint is billed per request. Failed requests, including `404`, are never charged; `meta.credit` reports the cost and your estimated remaining balance.

post.description:
Returns the current quotes for a list of items in one call. Each item's quotes follow the same rules as `GET /prices`: at most one per market and side, listed quotes preferred over delisted ones, then marketplace-sourced data over aggregators, then the freshest, plus the item's `CSCP` valuation (`side` `mid`) when it has one.

- `items` has one entry per requested name, in request order.
- Unknown names are not an error: they come back with an empty `markets` list. This endpoint never returns `404`.
- Duplicate names are kept, and each occurrence gets its own entry.
- `markets` and `side` filter every item the same way.
- Unknown fields in the request body are rejected with `422`.

> [!note]
> Billed per started block of item names, counted over the full `market_hash_names` list including duplicates. The cost is checked before the lookup (`402` if your balance is too low) and charged only when the request succeeds.

get.description:
Downloads the quotes of every priced item of one game as one file, for bulk synchronization. `side` defaults to `ask`; `side=mid` exports only the `CSCP` valuation of every valued item, a much smaller file.

- The body is the export document itself (`app_id`, `side`, `generated_at`, `items`), gzip-compressed (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) — not the usual envelope. The request id and the billing fields are response headers instead: `X-Request-ID`, `X-Billable`, and on a billed response `X-Credit-Cost` and `X-Credit-Remaining`.
- `items` lists every item with at least one quote on the requested side, ordered by market hash name; each item's quotes follow the same rules as `GET /prices`.
- The file is a snapshot rebuilt on the server every few minutes; `generated_at` (also the `X-Export-Generated-At` header) says when. Requests in between receive the same file.
- Send the `ETag` you received back as `If-None-Match`: while the snapshot is unchanged the answer is `304 Not Modified` with no body, and a `304` is never billed.
- `Range` requests are not supported; the whole file is always sent. There is no pagination or market filter.
- `503 dependency_unavailable` means the first snapshot has not been built yet; retry after a minute.

> [!warning]
> Every `200` is billed, even when the file has not changed. Poll with `If-None-Match` and you only pay when there is something new.

get.description:
Returns the fees the platform currently publishes for one marketplace, one slot per purpose: `deposit`, `sale` and `withdraw`.

- Each published slot carries the fully expanded official calculation chain: every fee operator, convert operator and convert operator group with its values and currencies, so one request is enough to reproduce the platform's calculation.
- A slot whose chain has `id` `0` is explicitly free: the platform charges nothing for that purpose, and the chain has no steps.
- A slot is `null` when the platform has no official calculation chain published for that purpose: the fee is unknown, or the marketplace does not offer it. `null` never means free.
- Each chain states its `start_currency`: the currency a price must be in for the chain to apply (`null`: any currency).
- Ownership and management fields are not included.

A `404` means no marketplace has this code.

get.description:
Returns what the API currently knows about your own account: profile fields including `base_currency` (the currency your calculations convert into; `null` means USD), the subscription active at the moment of the request (`null` when none), and your credit counters.

- `credit.total` is every credit granted to the account, `credit.used` what has been consumed, and `credit.remaining` the difference, never below `0`.
- These are the figures billing is applied against. They follow changes made in the dashboard within about a minute.

A `404` means your account has not reached the API yet; retry shortly.

Returns public, non-sensitive service configuration. Currently this is only `home_currency`, the platform currency that official calculation chains convert their results back into.

- Your own base currency is an account setting and is not returned here.
- Responses are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Returns machine-readable metadata for every documented operation of this API, so a client can plan its usage without parsing the OpenAPI document.

- One entry per method and path, sorted by path and then method.
- Each entry gives the credit cost (`credit_cost`, plus `unit_pricing` for operations billed by item count), whether it is `premium`, the suggested polling interval (`recommended_interval_seconds`), the `rate_limit`, and who may call it (`roles`: `user`, `admin`, `machine`; empty means no authentication is required).
- The same data appears in the OpenAPI document as the `x-cscheap` extension of each operation.

Lightweight liveness probe: returns `{"status": "ok"}` whenever the API process is up and serving requests.

- It checks no databases or other dependencies, so a `200` here does not guarantee that data endpoints are available. Use `GET /status` for service health history.
- The body is returned as-is, without the usual `data` / `meta` envelope.

Returns the service health and data-collection activity shown on the public status page: hourly health scores for the last 24 completed hours, per-component availability, price collection counts, and the geographic footprint of the collection network.

- Unlike `GET /health`, this reads recorded monitoring data; it is a history view, not a live probe of each dependency.
- Timestamps are UTC. Components or buckets with no data are empty or absent rather than zero.
- `503` means the monitoring data could not be read; partial results are never returned.
